text:
maya (AE): Hey team, jupiter is ready to start a Private deployment POC. They asked for guidance on the network onramp: their architecture is on‑prem -> SDWAN -> TGW -> customer VPC. Key asks: preserve client source IP for request-level attribution, static egress IP(s) for allowlisting, and whether we recommend VPC peering vs PrivateLink. Also pricing q: does Private deployment with a single EIP for egress change the Dedicated pricing vs hosted?

sam (SE): Congrats on the POC. Short answers: PrivateLink (interface endpoint) gives simpler onboarding + no cross-account routing rules, but you lose original TCP source IP at the application layer; peering/TGW preserves src IP. For static egress you can either: 1) put an NLB with fixed EIP in front of the Connector / proxy, or 2) SNAT at the TGW/NAT GW level. Both are OK; option 1 tends to be simpler for allowlist. Pricing: Dedicated/Private pricing is driven by reserved capacity and infra; the extra EIP or NAT costs are standard cloud egress charges — we don't charge extra for a single static egress IP, but Dedicated size (vCPU/GPU pool) is the main line item.

maria (NetOps): +1 to sam. A couple gotchas:
- If you use AWS Interface Endpoint (PrivateLink), the endpoint sits in your subnet and terminates TLS => endpoint will source traffic from its IPs, so backend sees endpoint ENI IPs, not original client IP. You can preserve identity by forwarding X‑Forwarded‑For from the proxy.
- If the customer requires TCP source IP preservation for mutual TLS client cert mapping, peering/TGW is the only straightforward option.
- Firewall rules: allow outbound 443 to our control-plane and model endpoints. If you want to restrict by IP, we can provide the egress IPs for the POC. Sample SG snippet:```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0abc123 --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 3.14.159.0/32
```

tony (Security): From a compliance perspective: provide the security questionnaire and we can confirm SOC2 scope and KMS integration. For PII/PCI workloads we'll need explicit network separation + customer-managed KMS and syslog/audit forwarding. Also confirm whether logs may cross regions — some customers require regional residency.

maya (AE): @sam can you confirm whether the POC can run with a single NLB + EIP in front of the connector so they can keep their existing firewall allowlist? Customer wants minimum changes to their edge.

sam (SE): Yes — recommended pattern: customer NAT -> NLB (BYOIP/EIP mapped) -> connector (in private subnets). That preserves a stable egress IP and keeps connector behind customer controls. If they need source IP on the backend (for mTLS), run connector in their VPC and use TGW peering so traffic never hits interface endpoints.

maria (NetOps): Ops note: if they terminate TLS at NLB and we need client certs, terminate TLS at customer proxy and re‑establish TLS to our service with mutual auth; otherwise you can't forward cert-level identity intact.

deploy-bot: POC provisioning ticket created: PROD‑POC‑3127. Reserved a small Dedicated pool (2x A10g equiv) for 7 days in us‑west‑2. Egress IP placeholders: 3.14.159.42 and 3.14.159.43 (subject to final allocation).

maya (AE): Thanks — action items: (1) sam to draft short diagram (NLB + connector vs TGW peering) and an ops checklist (ports, subnets, expected egress IPs), (2) ton y to accept preliminary security questionnaire, (3) maya to send customer the network runbook and set a 30‑min kickoff for Tuesday.

sam (SE): I'll drop the diagram + a one‑pager in this thread by EOD. Also attaching recommended firewall rule list: allow outbound 443 to the egress IPs, allow control plane 443, and open ephemeral ports for intra‑connector health checks (TCP 10250‑10255).

maya (AE): Great — looping in customer contact (jupiter-netops) on next msg and scheduling the kickoff. :thumbsup:
